name: Subliminals for appearance

lead: Appearance subliminals are audio recordings that supposedly carry hidden affirmations below conscious hearing, with listeners hoping for features like extra height, a different eye colour, jaw growth or less hair loss. They circulate on looksmaxxing forums and on subreddits dedicated to the practice.

Believers say the subconscious mind can be influenced by sub-audible affirmations. Laboratory research on subliminal stimuli has found effects on brain activity and on actions a person already intends to take, with limited, context-dependent results. No study has tested these recordings for physical change, and one self-concept trial found effects resembling placebo apart from a self-concept change.

paras: Listeners play tracks, often layered under music, for long stretches each day or while sleeping, over weeks to months. Forum members are split between those reporting results and those who attribute them to expectation.
Direct physical risk is low. Wikipedia notes subliminal advertising is prohibited in several countries.

angle.text: Listeners play subliminal audio hoping to grow taller, change eye colour, improve jaw growth or reduce hair loss through the subconscious. No study has tested physical change from these recordings, and forum members are split, with some crediting expectation.

lead: Subliminal audio, in the form used by looksmaxxing and self-improvement communities, consists of recordings that supposedly carry affirmations or intentions below the threshold of conscious hearing, often layered under music or sound, and are listened to in the hope of changing the body, such as growing taller, changing eye colour, improving jaw growth or reducing hair loss. Listeners claim these recordings work by influencing the subconscious mind.

Wikipedia defines subliminal stimuli as sensory stimuli below an individual's threshold for conscious perception, including audio played below audible volume or masked by other sounds [1]. Laboratory research has found effects of such stimuli on brain activity and on actions a person already intends to take, but the American Psychological Association was reported in 2009 as saying there was no conclusive evidence that effects are truly subliminal [1].
No study found has tested subliminal audio for changing physical appearance. Forum threads show a mix of users reporting results, users citing placebo, and users who say the idea does not work.
infobox: Height, eye colour, jaw growth, hair, attractiveness
Audio tracks, often listened to while sleeping

paras: Appearance subliminals are audio files marketed or shared for a specific physical outcome. Thread titles show targets such as growing taller while sleeping, eye colour change, growth of both jaws and hair loss. One forum poster says the community has gone from cold showers and mewing through surgeries and back to subliminals. Another refers to the subreddit r/subliminals, where members make extreme claims of results.

The idea of covert persuasion became popular after cinematographer James Vicary claimed in 1957 that hidden messages in films boosted soft drink sales; Wikipedia says he later admitted inflating the results [1]. Later research found that subliminal stimuli can activate brain regions without awareness and may prime actions a person already plans to take, and a meta-analysis found no significant effect on consumer choice between two alternatives [1]. Wikipedia describes one study where thirsty participants primed with a drink brand chose it more often, but characterises it as limited [1].

Wikipedia also summarises a study of 141 undergraduates with self-concept problems randomised to rational-emotive therapy, subliminal stimulation, both or placebo. The subliminal group looked like the placebo group except for a significant improvement in self-concept and fewer related irrational cognitions [1]. The page describes the effect as limited to self-concept and does not report any physical measure.

No studies found on subliminal audio for height, facial structure, hair, eye colour or other physical appearance. General subliminal-perception research and one study of subliminal self-concept recordings exist, but they address psychological rather than physical outcomes [1].

Forum threads have titles claiming positive results, asking whether subliminals work, and proposing that any effect might act through placebo. A results thread invited users to report outcomes. Some posters say they listen to subliminals for height gain while asleep. Others say they are sceptical but ask why so many users on a subreddit report extreme results.

lore.intro: On looksmax.org subliminals are a recurring, contested topic, with threads for and against and frequent suggestion of a placebo explanation.
